6.2 Findings:
1. (Bug, fixed this cycle) The "BOM Line Items" and "Approval Summary" grids on the Summary tab, and the grid in the "Review for Approval" dialog, rendered header-only with no visible rows: each one's <wfx-surface> wrapper collapsed to 0 height because it sat inside a non-flex ancestor (a <wfx-panel> body or a dialog body) with no definite height to resolve its own flex:1;height:100% against. Corrected by giving each wfx-surface an explicit [minHeight] (320px / 200px / 360px to match each grid) and the grid itself height="100%".
2. (Bug, fixed this cycle) Duplicating two or more sizes at once could silently drop a child kit record: the dialog saved every new child in parallel, which raced against the mock server's unlocked read-modify-write file I/O, and the loser's write was overwritten before it could persist — though the dialog reported success for every size. Corrected by saving children one at a time, sequentially, never in parallel.
3. (Bug, fixed this cycle) The Summary tab's own content (Kit Information + BOM Line Items + Totals + Approval Summary) is taller than the viewport once a master kit has duplicated children, but the page could not be scrolled far enough to reach the bottom: the tab's wrapping stack had no overflow handling of its own, while the page-level container intentionally disables page-level scrolling for this "grid fills the viewport" tab style (used by the other, single-grid tabs). Corrected by adding vertical scroll to this one tab's own wrapping stack.
4. (Bug, fixed this cycle) Delete used to run with no confirmation, no eligibility check, and never cleaned up a master's duplicated children (left them pointing at a ParentId that no longer existed). Corrected: Delete now confirms first (stating the child count up front), is hidden entirely on an Approved kit, and cascades to delete all of a master's children in the same action.
5. (Standards gap, fixed this cycle) The list's "Created" column header has been renamed to "Created On", matching the studio convention of naming the header after the field.
6. (Standards gap, fixed this cycle) The list's Total Cost column was marked non-sortable with no technical reason (it is an ordinary client-side valueGetter column); it now sorts like any other numeric column.
7. (Standards gap, open) The Additional Cost tab's Currency column is a free-text cell, while the otherwise-identical Packing Materials tab's Currency column is a proper select from the same currency list (see the Additional Cost screenshot). Recommended: make Additional Cost's Currency a select too, for the same reason Packing Materials already is — a typo currency code shouldn't be able to corrupt a cost line. See Open Question Q-3.
8. (Missing validation, open) Order Qty Expected has no visible inline validation — it silently blocks "Create Kit" via the enablement gate, but nothing on the field itself tells the user why. Recommend an inline Signal Forms required() / min() validator consistent with the kit's other seed fields.

chunks.title: 1 Overview
chunks.heading: 1 Overview
chunks.text:
The Kit/Pack BOM & Costing screen lets a merchandiser or costing team build the bill of materials and cost sheet for a kitted or packed product — a single sellable unit made of several garments and/or packaging articles (e.g. a boys' 5-pack tee combo, a girls' polo assortment across sizes). It lives under Catalog › Kit/Pack Management in the ERP product studio.
On one kit record, the user defines the component articles and their colour/size breakdown, the packing materials, a routing process, and any additional charges; the screen rolls all of that up into a Total Cost, and the user enters a Selling Price to see the resulting Profit % and Markup %. Once the costing is agreed, the kit is Approved, which locks it. A kit can also be duplicated into one linked child kit per size variant, and a master kit's family (itself plus every duplicated child) can be reviewed and approved together.
Primary users: merchandising / costing team (build and price the kit), approver (reviews the family and approves).

chunks.title: 4 Workflow & status lifecycle
chunks.heading: 4 Workflow & status lifecycle
chunks.text:
States: (not yet created) → Open → Approved.
• Not yet created — only the Kit/Pack tab is usable; "Create Kit" is enabled once every required field on it is filled (plus Order Qty Expected > 0); tabs 2–6 stay disabled until then.
• Open — every field on every tab is editable and auto-saves on change; "Approve" is available.
• Approved — every field on every tab becomes read-only (header fields, all four grids, Routing, Selling Price/Discount %); the Approve button shows "Approved" and is disabled. There is no path back to Open (no un-approve action) — see Open Question Q-5.
• Approving a master also auto-approves every duplicated child whose own Pack Items breakdown is an unmodified copy of the master's data for the size(s) it carries, whose Packing Materials/Routing/Additional Cost are identical to the master's, and whose Selling Price matches the master's exactly ("same items, materials, FOB and Margin"). A child that doesn't match this stays Open and must be approved individually from its own detail page.
chunks.locator: § 4 Workflow & status lifecycle

chunks.title: 4 Workflow & status lifecycle
chunks.heading: 4 Workflow & status lifecycle
chunks.text:
• Delete is offered only on an Open kit (mirrors the real sales-order list's "Delete only when Saved" convention) and requires confirmation. Deleting a master cascades to delete every one of its duplicated children in the same action, with the confirm message stating the exact count up front. An Approved kit cannot be deleted, and there is no separate Cancel-with-reason flow.
• Duplicate is offered only from a master row — a duplicated child can never itself be duplicated further (one level of nesting only).

chunks.title: 6.1 Mock shortcuts
chunks.heading: 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.1 Mock shortcuts
chunks.text:
• One committed record holds the kit's header, full BOM and costing fields together — the real app splits these across separate article/BOM/cost-sheet tables.
• Tabs 2–6 are locked behind a manual "Create Kit" button instead of the studio's usual auto-create-on-seed-fields pattern — deliberate, mirroring both the source PDF spec and the real wfx-kit-pack-detail screen's own convention.
• The Summary tab's BOM Line Items list is flat, not a tree: the real screen's "MATERIAL" child rows come from the linked article's own Manufacturing BOM, which is out of scope until that screen exists — here Manufacturing BOM is a free-text field, not a real link.
• BMV and EPM are static 0.00 placeholders — the product team has not yet defined their formula (Open Question Q-1).
• A duplicated kit is exactly one level of nesting — a child can never itself be duplicated.
• "Copy From" is present in the UI but not implemented.
• Routing/Processes models a single process + rate, not a sequence of routing steps.
• All grids are client-side (no server paging) — fine at today's record counts; flag for server-side paging once volume grows (QA checklist §6).
chunks.locator: § 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.1 Mock shortcuts

chunks.title: 6.2 Findings
chunks.heading: 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings
chunks.text:
• (Bug, fixed this cycle) The "BOM Line Items" and "Approval Summary" grids on the Summary tab, and the grid in the "Review for Approval" dialog, rendered header-only with no visible rows: each one's <wfx-surface> wrapper collapsed to 0 height because it sat inside a non-flex ancestor (a <wfx-panel> body or a dialog body) with no definite height to resolve its own flex:1;height:100% against. Corrected by giving each wfx-surface an explicit [minHeight] (320px / 200px / 360px to match each grid) and the grid itself height="100%".
• (Bug, fixed this cycle) Duplicating two or more sizes at once could silently drop a child kit record: the dialog saved every new child in parallel, which raced against the mock server's unlocked read-modify-write file I/O, and the loser's write was overwritten before it could persist — though the dialog reported success for every size. Corrected by saving children one at a time, sequentially, never in parallel.
chunks.locator: § 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings

chunks.title: 6.2 Findings
chunks.heading: 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings
chunks.text:
• (Bug, fixed this cycle) The Summary tab's own content (Kit Information + BOM Line Items + Totals + Approval Summary) is taller than the viewport once a master kit has duplicated children, but the page could not be scrolled far enough to reach the bottom: the tab's wrapping stack had no overflow handling of its own, while the page-level container intentionally disables page-level scrolling for this "grid fills the viewport" tab style (used by the other, single-grid tabs). Corrected by adding vertical scroll to this one tab's own wrapping stack.
• (Bug, fixed this cycle) Delete used to run with no confirmation, no eligibility check, and never cleaned up a master's duplicated children (left them pointing at a ParentId that no longer existed). Corrected: Delete now confirms first (stating the child count up front), is hidden entirely on an Approved kit, and cascades to delete all of a master's children in the same action.
• (Standards gap, fixed this cycle) The list's "Created" column header has been renamed to "Created On", matching the studio convention of naming the header after the field.
• (Standards gap, fixed this cycle) The list's Total Cost column was marked non-sortable with no technical reason (it is an ordinary client-side valueGetter column); it now sorts like any other numeric column.
chunks.locator: § 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings (part 2)

chunks.title: 6.2 Findings
chunks.heading: 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings
chunks.text:
• (Standards gap, open) The Additional Cost tab's Currency column is a free-text cell, while the otherwise-identical Packing Materials tab's Currency column is a proper select from the same currency list (see the Additional Cost screenshot). Recommended: make Additional Cost's Currency a select too, for the same reason Packing Materials already is — a typo currency code shouldn't be able to corrupt a cost line. See Open Question Q-3.
• (Missing validation, open) Order Qty Expected has no visible inline validation — it silently blocks "Create Kit" via the enablement gate, but nothing on the field itself tells the user why. Recommend an inline Signal Forms required() / min() validator consistent with the kit's other seed fields.
• (Missing validation / dead field, open) Discount % is captured on the Summary tab but is never read by any Total Cost, Selling Price, Profit % or Markup % calculation in wfx-kit-pack.util.ts — it currently has no effect. See Open Question Q-2.
• (UX, open) Pack Items, Packing Materials and Additional Cost show no empty-state message when a freshly-created kit has zero rows — just a blank grid body under the "Add …" button. Recommend the studio's shared empty-state pattern ("No items yet — click Add Item to add one.").
chunks.locator: § 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings (part 3)

chunks.title: 6.2 Findings
chunks.heading: 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings
chunks.text:
• (Standards gap, open) Money values are shown as a plain formatted number with the currency code named only in the column/field header (e.g. "Total Cost (VND)"), never a currency symbol on the value itself — the studio standard (QA checklist §2) calls for both. Low severity since the code is always visible one column/label away, but worth a conscious decision rather than an oversight.
• (UX, open) The "SKU Description" column header reads just "SKU Description" in the Review for Approval dialog but "Kit SKU Description" in the Summary tab's Approval Summary grid — same field, two labels. Recommend picking one wording and using it in both places.
chunks.locator: § 6 Out-of-scope & deltas › 6.2 Findings (part 4)

chunks.title: 7 Open questions
chunks.heading: 7 Open questions
chunks.text:
• What is the BMV and EPM formula for the Summary tab's totals card and Approval Summary grid? Currently static 0.00 placeholders. Owner: Product team.
• Should Discount % actually affect the costing math (Selling Price, Profit %, Markup %), and if so how — applied before or after Markup is computed? See Finding F-9. Owner: Product team.
• Should Additional Cost's Currency be a select (matching Packing Materials) instead of free text? See Finding F-7. Owner: Product team / Dev lead.
• Is there an upper bound on Packing Materials' Wastage %, or a maximum number of colors/sizes a Pack Items parent row may carry? Owner: Product team.
• Does an Approved kit ever need to be reopened (e.g. a costing error found after approval), and if so what audit trail does that need? There is currently no path back from Approved. Owner: Product team.
• What should happen if two users duplicate the same size from the same master at nearly the same time (two "L" children created from one master in quick succession)? Nothing in the client or the mock server currently prevents this. Owner: Product team / Dev lead.
